content_voiceover: Before you can call something immune thrombocytopenia, you have to earn that diagnosis by excluding mimics, and this table is the board-style checklist for doing that. Number one, always first, is pseudothrombocytopenia from EDTA-dependent platelet agglutinins, an artifact with zero clinical importance but a trap if you miss it. Next, think about drug, herbal, or food-induced thrombocytopenia, especially if a patient has recurrent acute episodes rather than one persistent low count. Screen for HIV, which causes isolated thrombocytopenia in advanced disease and improves with antiretroviral therapy, and for hepatitis C, which can drive immune-mediated platelet destruction. Don't forget systemic lupus and lymphoproliferative disorders, which can mimic ITP serologically but need different primary treatment. Myelodysplasia can present with isolated thrombocytopenia alone, so a bone marrow exam matters in the right clinical context. The high-yield trap is TTP, which classically presents with only thrombocytopenia and anemia, no fever, no neuro findings, and the anemia gets misattributed to bleeding, so always check a smear for schistocytes before anchoring on ITP. Finally, consider congenital or hereditary thrombocytopenia, particularly in young patients who fail to respond to standard ITP therapy.
keypoints: TTP can look like isolated thrombocytopenia + anemia, no neuro signs
HIV and HCV both cause immune-mediated thrombocytopenia
SLE, MDS, drug-induced ITP are key mimickers
Refractory ITP in young patients → consider congenital thrombocytopenia
keypoint_voiceover: Five things to burn in before calling it ITP. Pseudothrombocytopenia is excluded first, every time, it's just an EDTA artifact. TTP is the dangerous mimic, it can look like isolated thrombocytopenia plus anemia with no neurologic signs at all. Screen HIV and hepatitis C, both cause immune-mediated low platelets. Keep lupus, myelodysplasia, and drug-induced thrombocytopenia on your differential. And if a young patient isn't responding to ITP treatment, think congenital thrombocytopenia.
